scope: Corollary 4.5 (Sieve and cosieve covers after attachment) of the manuscript “Thomason Model Structures in Every Strict Higher Dimension” (preprints/Thomason-Model-Structures-in-Every-Strict-Higher-Dimension-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 317 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4297861df49692b8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 16-17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: With the notation of Proposition 4.4, the following are canonical identifications of subcategories of Y . (i) Suppose P1, P2 are sieves of P, contain A, and cover P. Then the subcategories Yi = X ⨿UA UPi (i = 1, 2) are sieves covering Y on objects, and Y1 ∩ Y2 = X ⨿UA UP1∩P2 . 16 (ii) Suppose T1, T2 are cosieves of P, cover P, satisfy A ⊂ T1, and satisfy A ∩ T2 = ∅. Then Y1 = X ⨿UA UT1 , Y2 = UT2 are cosieves covering Y on objects, and Y1 ∩ Y2 = UT1∩T2 . If A itself is a sieve of P, the canonical map X → Y is the inclusion of a full sieve.
